title: Notorious - Have Blaster, Will Travel (solo RPG)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDDnbn7KVls

On solo RPG Friday, Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at Notorious by Jason Price, a Kickstarter-delivered solo game of space bounty hunting that he calls a space western and recommends especially for beginners. The reason is structure. Your Nomad works for one of six factions on one of six planets, and every session follows the same loop: roll on the exploration table, roll on the destination table, resolve an encounter, repeat until you have found three leads. The third lead is the target, the showdown follows, then an epilogue, and the whole thing runs about ninety minutes to two hours.

A reaction chart governs everything you meet. Locals and assets can be spoken to or recruited, hostiles threatened or attacked, leads and targets spoken to or attacked, and combat is a quick duel rather than a war of attrition. Notoriety, favour and motivation are the only stats, and the first two rise as you kill or persuade, improving your odds of finding leads. Six classes include a bot, which is what Daniel plays: DD-720, hired by the Red Moon Syndicate to stop an insectoid named Picto-Click whose hive tunnels are undermining a crypto casino. Origin, scar and trigger prompts colour the character without mechanics, and because the book has no oracle he brought fate dice for yes-or-no questions.

He praises the spiral binding, the muted art and the guild code, and would play it as episodic one-shots with fresh hunters rather than a campaign.

----

Notorious gives you a strict loop and no oracle, leaving the story to you. Do you prefer solo RPGs that supply structure or ones that supply prompts?
